records.subject: Labour, Employment, Wages and Productivity
records.title: Workplace Injury Rate, Annual
records.footnote: A workplace injury is any personal injury or death resulting from a workplace accident, including work-related traffic injuries.  A work-related traffic accident is any unintended event that causes bodily injury to a vocational driver or rider while he or she is driving any vehicle in the course of work.  Prior to January 2021, the data for workplace injury only covered injuries sustained by employees that resulted in four or more days of medical leave, or at least 24 hours of hospitalisation.  Following the amendments to the Work   Injury Compensation Act (WICA) which took effect from September 2020, employers need to report all work injuries with any instance of medical leave or light duties.  From 2021, the data pertaining to all non-fatal injuries with any instance of medical leave or light duties are denoted by [N].   Data are used for SDG 8.8.1 'Fatal and non-fatal occupational injuries per 100,000 workers, by sex and migrant status'.  Please refer to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Global Metadata (https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata) for more information on SDG 8.8.1.
